_note: Per iOS screen (SweepFrames.swift names): its Android status (not-ported, in-progress, parity) and the differences still open. Read by scripts/android_parity.py. DECISIONS.md 2026-11-10.

_android_forced.why: SF Symbols exist only on Apple platforms; Android uses Material Symbols, the matching glyph each time (map, search, eco leaf, photo_camera).
Android has no system material blur for what lies under a view; the grey glass is the ground at 92 percent with the iPhone's 6 percent ink wash.
Android's system back gesture and button close the top sheet or page, as every Android app does.
The location and camera questions are the system's own dialogs.
Google instead of Apple; Sign in with Apple does not exist on Android.
Android's own bars at the top and bottom of the screen.
SF Pro, the iPhone's system face, exists only on Apple platforms; Android's own system face (Roboto) stands in at the same sizes and weights. The brand face Gabarito is the same on both.
The share circle on a tree's card opens Android's share sheet with the same tagged link (utm_campaign=map_card).
The Species chip's list is a system sheet on both phones: SwiftUI's .sheet on the iPhone, Material's modal bottom sheet on Android.

The iPhone asks once between Apple Maps and Google Maps and remembers it; Android has no Apple Maps, so its place in the same question is Another maps app, which hands the spot to Android's own chooser (a geo: link that Waze, OsmAnd and every maps app answer). Google Maps opens the same walking-route link as on the iPhone.
The report menu on a tree page is the system's own pop-up menu on both phones: SwiftUI's Menu on the iPhone, Material's dropdown menu on Android.
Android's bottom sheet runs the full width of the screen with its own drag handle; the iPhone's sheet on iOS 26 floats with a margin. Content, sizes and order are the same.

Android's photo picker removes a photograph's location before the app sees it, so a photograph chosen from the library always asks where the tree stands (the iPhone reads it off the photograph). The camera path is the same on both.
The iPhone keeps a copy on the phone and sends it in the background; Android keeps nothing on the phone (hard rule 11), so it sends at once and says so when it did not arrive.
Open Settings lands on the app's own page in Android's Settings, and the recovery sheet's path line names Android's path; Rate the app opens the Play Store.
The iPhone's Yes opens Apple's rating dialog; Android's opens Google Play's own review card (the Play review library), the platform's equivalent.

differences: Waiting on iOS, not an Android gap: Build 42's Airbnb sheet (LOG.md 2026-11-08: only the count bar at the lowest stop, the tab bar hidden) is decided but not in the iPhone's Swift on main yet; Android follows the Swift and takes it when it lands.
First launch reads the 11.5 MB catalogue in about ten seconds on the one-core emulator under a loaded Mac; later launches read a binary snapshot. Not yet measured on a real phone.
Under a searched city the ambassador and Plus boxes (PlaceAsksBox, PlusUnderBox) are not ported yet (sessions 5 and 6).

Your own trees stand on the map in your own photograph and lead the Collected shelf (TreeMap.setMine, MineTile); the photograph comes from the account each launch, so a new install shows the plain mine pin until it has loaded (hard rule 11).
As map.
As map; the share circle opens Android's share sheet (forced). The card is now TreeCard ported whole (TreeRows.kt), its words in every language.
Recent searches (signed in, kept on the server) are not ported yet.
A town we have no trees in (Apple's MKLocalSearch on the iPhone) is not looked up yet; Android says nothing matches.
The on-screen keyboard shows on Android; the iPhone simulator types from the Mac's keyboard, so its shot has none. Both focus the field.
The review prompt after three trees and the tree_opened measurement are not ported (session 8).
Collect: Remove from collected (with Undo) in the collect sheet is not ported yet.
The snackbar after a bookmark: Added to Want to visit with View, Removed with Undo, as SaveHeart.swift (SnackBar.kt).
As tree.
Continue with Apple is not there (forced: Sign in with Apple does not exist on Android); Google and email are the iPhone's pills, sizes and order.
A failed ambassador request says so in a one-line BrandSheet, where the iPhone shows the snackbar: Android has no shared snackbar yet (as city).

A card face with no website choice falls back to the first photographed tree; the iPhone's fallback also weighs the photograph's size, which the Android feed reader does not read yet. The feed carries a face for every shelf today, so nothing shows this.
Pull to refresh is Material's spinner, the Android counterpart of the iPhone's refresh control (forced).
The map tiles may still be loading in the Android frame (screenshot timing, not layout).
Your own trees show as species pins on the map, not as your photograph in the pin (TreeMapView has no own-photo pin yet; map session's piece).
Tapping your own pin shows our card without your photograph on it (TreePlaceBody has no ownPhoto yet).
The gear, your name and photo, Find people and the follower counts open the account sheet until Profile, ProfileEditor and People are ported (android-parity-7-profile).
The ambassador and early-adopter tags under the name are not drawn yet (Badges.kt comes with the profile session).
Signed out on a small phone the sheet stays at half rather than the card stop.
The mission's location-off chip is not drawn when the location is unknown.

Ancient Trees Plus is the first row under Help, as on the iPhone (Profile.swift helpCard): it opens the city's Plus question (PlaceBox.kt PlusQuestionSheet, from PlusAsk.swift), sends the anonymous answer to plus_answers and Tell me to plus_waitlist, and the row goes once this install answered (plus.answered.v1, device) or the server's switch is off. -plusask opens it.
Distances follows the phone's region until chosen, as on the iPhone; the emulator stands in the US, so it reads Miles where the simulator reads Kilometres.
Directions offers Google Maps and Another maps app (no Apple Maps on Android, forced).
Rate the app opens the Play Store page (forced).
Delete photo (for your own photographs) comes with My trees (session 4).
Your own trees within 30 m are drawn and add the photograph to that tree, but only once MainActivity passes mine = myTrees and openMine to CollectHost (wiring pending).
The App Store style review ask two seconds after a new tick is not ported (session 8).
Move the pin and Merge with another tree are not in the draft's menu yet: their screens (place-pin, MergeChooser) are not ported, as on own-tree.

After Save the page waits a moment for the account to hold the tree before it turns into your tree with Share: the iPhone keeps it on the phone first, Android keeps nothing a person did on the device (hard rule 11).
The city link and the page staying as your tree after Save need MainActivity to pass account, mine and onCity to DraftTree (wiring pending).
The sheet at full height is 96 percent opaque on Android (MapSheet), so the map shows faintly behind the list; the iPhone's page is solid.
The white discs behind the gear and Find people vanish on the white sheet; the iPhone's sheet is a shade greyer.

Ancient Trees Plus is the first row under Help, as on the iPhone (Profile.swift helpCard): it opens the city's Plus question (PlaceBox.kt PlusQuestionSheet, from PlusAsk.swift), sends the anonymous answer to plus_answers and Tell me to plus_waitlist, and the row goes once this install answered (plus.answered.v1, device) or the server's switch is off. -plusask opens it.
Distances follows the phone's region until chosen, as on the iPhone; the emulator stands in the US, so it reads Miles where the simulator reads Kilometres.
As profile: Directions offers Google Maps and Another maps app, Rate the app opens the Play Store (forced).

The map's place header, its Highlights and Collected shelves, the white box with the ambassador row and the Plus box under the trees, ported from PlaceAmbassadors.swift, AmbassadorBadge.swift and PlusAsk.swift (PlaceBox.kt). A failed ambassador request says so on the one sheet: Android has no shared snackbar yet.
As city. The faint circle under the grip is the shared MapSheet's, as on map-full (coordinator's).

SpeciesPage.kt from Species.swift: mark, name, Latin in italics, count, the species paragraph, photographed trees first then nearest. Android's back arrow in the bar (forced). Reached from a tree page's species, Discover's species tiles and its See all list.
CollectionView in Home.swift: the intro, then every tree as the shared TreeCard. The back arrow in the bar and the system back are Android's (forced).

PlacePin.kt from PlacePin.swift: the map moves under a fixed pin, the arrow above the card, the card's words and the disabled button until the pin moved 5 m. The crosshair is the Material map pin (PinPicker.kt, shared with collect). The map's licence credit (i) stays visible in the bottom corner. System back is Cancel (forced).
Move the pin and Merge with another tree are not in the menu yet: their screens (place-pin, MergeChooser) are not ported.
Naming the species uses the map's species picker, not SpeciesChooser (species-pick, not ported).
The hero keeps a 3:4 portrait shape for every photograph; the iPhone takes the photograph's own shape.
Share sends the link only; the iPhone also hands on a drawn share card (ShareCard.swift).

SpeciesChooser.kt from SpeciesChooser.swift, now also on your own tree and the draft: grouped list, matched name and Latin under each row, Not on the map yet, Use what you typed, the search field at the foot. Close is the bar's plain text as in every ported sheet (BarSheet), where iOS 26 draws a capsule. The map's Species filter (SpeciesPicker.kt) uses the same list.

notes: The question before Google's card is kept as on the iPhone (Hidde, 2026-11-10: "prima doe dat"), though Google's guide asks for none; it sits behind the remote switch android_review_question in data/app-switches.json, so it can be turned off without a build if Google ever objects. Off, the card comes at the same moments without the question.

differences: As signin: the iPhone's -show-email draws the same sheet; Continue with email opens the field and Email me a sign-in link, then Check your email with Open Gmail or Open Mail chosen by the address.
The path line names Android's own Settings path (Settings › Apps › Ancient Trees › Permissions › Location), and Open Settings lands on the app's own page there (forced).
The signed-in form (the four kinds and Where) has no sweep frame on either phone; it was looked at on Android with -signed-in, not side by side.
The flag is the system's flag emoji in a circle; the iPhone fills the circle with the website's flat flag (flag-icons). Same on My trees and a person's profile.
The editor is a full-height bottom sheet with Cancel and Save in its bar (the iPhone's Form sheet); the country list opens as a second sheet rather than a pushed list.
Pull to refresh on Find people loads who you follow and Suggested again (Material's pull to refresh, People.swift RefreshableWhen); Followers and Following keep still, as on the iPhone.
Blocked people are held in memory and read back from the server's blocks table; the iPhone also keeps the list on the phone (hard rule 11 on Android).
Share your profile opens Android's share sheet (forced).
The tags row (Paris ambassador, Early adopter) matches; the rest of the frame is My trees (collection-tab) and its differences are listed there.

_shared._note: Pieces every screen uses. One owner each; a screen session changes them only through its owner.
